question:
A plane monochromatic electromagnetic wave in air (normal incidence) falls on a thin transparent film of refractive index $n_f=\dfrac{3}{2}$ coated on a **high-index glass** plate of refractive index $n_g=2.25$. All media are non-magnetic and lossless.

For normal incidence, the amplitude reflection coefficients at an interface are
</br>$r_{12}=\dfrac{n_1-n_2}{n_1+n_2},\qquad r_{23}=\dfrac{n_2-n_3}{n_2+n_3}$</br>
and the net amplitude reflection coefficient of a single-layer film is
</br>$r=\dfrac{r_{12}+r_{23}e^{i\phi}}{1+r_{12}r_{23}e^{i\phi}},\qquad \phi=\dfrac{4\pi n_f t}{\lambda}$,</br>
where $\lambda$ is the wavelength in air.

The film is intended as an anti-reflection coating at $\lambda_0=600\,\text{nm}$, but to improve durability the designer chooses the **smallest thickness $t\ge 250\,\text{nm}$** that still gives **zero reflection** at $\lambda_0$.

For this chosen coating, among the given visible wavelengths, the reflected intensity fraction $\dfrac{I_R}{I_0}=|r|^2$ is maximum at which $\lambda$, and what is the closest value of $\dfrac{I_R}{I_0}$ at that wavelength?
